drafts.title: Front and rear seats deliver longer thigh support, durable cushioning and reliably restored memory positions
drafts.description: Customers experience seats that support tall drivers along the thigh, keep their shape over years of daily use, and restore saved positions reliably after vehicle start or profile selection.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Front-seat thigh support is extendable by at least 50 mm compared to current baseline; seat cushion thickness loss ≤10% after 1,000 standardized seating cycles; seat memory restores saved position within 10 mm linear / 1° angular of saved values on ≥99% of restore attempts within 30 seconds of vehicle start.
assumptions: 1,000 standardized seating cycles approximate 3–5 years of typical use for a 5-Series customer.
Baseline seat geometry refers to today's 5 Series; extension of thigh support by 50 mm is mechanically feasible within successor packaging.
Seat position sensors and actuators have resolution sufficient to measure 10 mm / 1°.
uncertainties: Longer thigh support and denser foam may affect seat weight and cost.
Real-world durability depends on upholstery choice and customer use patterns; lab cycles are an approximation.

drafts.title: Interior convenience features meet everyday needs: cup holders, ambient lighting and trunk power
drafts.description: Customers can store common bottles and travel mugs, personalise cabin ambience with many colors/brightness steps, and power portable appliances from the trunk.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Primary cup holders accommodate bottles up to 75 mm diameter and a common 16 oz (≈473 ml) travel mug simultaneously; ambient lighting offers at least 64 discrete colors and 8 independent brightness levels selectable for front and rear; trunk includes a 12 V power socket accessible with trunk open and capable of delivering up to 120 W (10 A) in 100% of vehicles.
assumptions: 75 mm diameter covers the majority (>90%) of common bottled-water and travel-mug profiles US customers carry.
12 V / 120 W is sufficient to run typical electric cooler boxes customers described.
Ambient-lighting colour granularity of 64 is perceived as a clearly broader palette by customers.
uncertainties: Power availability in trunk when vehicle is off depends on vehicle electrical architecture and battery-management strategy.
Larger cup holders may reduce console storage; trade-offs with other interior packaging exist.

drafts.title: Exterior access functions reliably in cold and with hands-free operation
drafts.description: Customers can open the hands-free tailgate reliably on the first attempt and can open flush door handles in freezing conditions without repeated attempts.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Hands-free tailgate opens on first standardized wave attempt (single forward wave within 3 seconds at the prescribed sensor area) in ≥95% of tests across a range of common footwear and load conditions; flush door handles operate successfully after 15 minutes of windblown-ice exposure at −20 °C in ≥98% of attempts.
assumptions: Standardized test protocols for 'first wave' and windblown-ice exposure are defined and repeatable in lab conditions.
Environmental tests reflect common northern U.S. winter conditions (down to −20 °C with ice accretion).
uncertainties: Extreme ice or aftermarket coatings may still cause failures; some scenarios require owner intervention.
Solutions may affect packaging and sealing details around handles and tailgate sensors.

drafts.title: Rear-seat legroom equals or exceeds main competitors’ segment average
drafts.description: Customers in the rear seat experience legroom that is at least as generous as the segment average so passengers do not feel cramped compared with rivals.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Measured rear knee clearance (distance from rear-seat knee point to front-seat back) is ≥ 940 mm when the front seat is set to a driving position representing the 95th-percentile driver; in a blinded in-vehicle comparator test, ≥95% of participants judge rear legroom as equal or better than the segment average competitor vehicles.
assumptions: Segment average knee clearance is approximately 940 mm for the main competitor set in the U.S. executive sedan segment at successor launch.
Front-seat 95th-percentile driving position is defined per SAE/ISO anthropometric standards used by BMW.
uncertainties: Achieving additional rear legroom may require packaging changes that impact trunk volume or front-seat geometry.
Competitor dimensions may change; acceptance relies on comparator set chosen at launch.

drafts.title: Physical volume control provides precise, reliable, eyes-free operation
drafts.description: Customers can adjust audio volume precisely and reliably using the physical control without needing to look at the screen.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In a blinded user test, 90% of participants can change volume by ±1 dB using the control without looking in no more than two blind rotations; the control reports no missed or duplicate steps in ≥99% of interactions during normal driving conditions.
assumptions: Perceptible 1 dB volume increments are meaningful to customers in typical in-car listening conditions.
Test participants cover a representative mix of ages and hand sizes for the U.S. market.
uncertainties: Implementation of the control (mechanical vs. haptic vs. software filtering) impacts how 'no missed steps' is achieved.
Integration with software volume scaling may affect perceived step size.

drafts.title: Perceptibly quieter cabin and improved perceived solidity from side glazing
drafts.description: Customers notice reduced exterior noise intrusion and a more solid feel from the vehicle side glazing and window assemblies.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: A-weighted interior sound level at 100 km/h on a smooth highway test track is reduced by at least 2 dB compared with the current model baseline; in a blinded panel test, ≥70% of participants rate external-noise intrusion as 'noticeably quieter.'
assumptions: Current-model baseline measurements are available for direct comparison in the same test conditions.
A >2 dB reduction is perceptible and meaningful to customers in the target segment.
Thicker/laminated side glass is one of several measures (glass, seals, door structure) contributing to the outcome.
uncertainties: Noise performance depends on multiple vehicle systems; attributing improvement to side glass alone is approximate.
Weight, cost and solar/thermal performance trade-offs may constrain glazing choices.
